claim: Adding a job to `gate` put it in `needs:` and not in the pass/fail loop, so `gate` would have waited for it, read its failure and reported success. `ci-changed.test.ts` failed the author's push and exposed it inside the branch; both lists are now derived from the workflow itself and pinned equal, and the derivation was mutation-checked to refuse.
boardClaim: The check that guards our main line can now be shown to refuse failing work, and it is no longer possible to extend it in a way that quietly cannot.
evidence: Every change we ship passes one automated check before it can join the main line, and that check cannot be waived by an administrator. It keeps two lists: what it waits for, and what it can fail for. Someone adding a new job put it in the first and not the second — so that job would have been waited for, seen to fail, and reported as a pass. **It never reached the main line.** A different check failed the author's own push and the fault it exposed was larger than the one it was looking for; the two commits carrying it existed only inside that branch. We examined every state the main line has ever been in — eighteen of them — and none had the gap. The fix makes the two lists read from one source, so they cannot disagree again, **and the guard was made to FAIL against the fault before it was trusted**: four earlier guards in this project shipped green against the very fault they were written for, and that demonstration is the difference. This is a statement about how the check is wired, not a re-run of past decisions — it does not claim that nothing faulty has ever merged, which is a larger question we have not asked. (`gate` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, issue #356 via PR #384, fixed by `worker-capture`; found by `ci-changed.test.ts`; trunk audit `git rev-list --first-parent origin/main -- ci.yml`, 18 states, 0 with the gap, run by `dispatcher` and re-derived by `product-manager`.)
affirmed: Re-verified 2026-09-09 at 07:16Z by dispatcher, on main at 7400a850, by running the derivation and then breaking it. `npx tsx --test packages/lab/src/packaging/ci-changed.test.ts` reports 44/44; `gate`'s two lists are still equal and still read out of the workflow rather than written twice -- `needs:` and the result-checking loop both carry the same eleven jobs (changed, ts, python, ansible, docs, board, changeset, rulesFitness, mergeSafety, acceptance, ownedPaths). Then the part that makes it a claim rather than a reading: `npm run mutate` adding a twelfth job to `needs:` and not to the loop -- the exact fault -- reports THE GUARD BITES. The claim stands as written. Two things it still does NOT say: nothing faulty has ever merged (a larger question nobody has asked), and nothing about jobs outside `gate` -- `audit` is not in that context, which is precisely how a red check sat on seven merged PRs for ninety minutes on 8 September without blocking anything.
